title: How much a GPS satellite clock drifts each day (microseconds per day)

source.name: Real-World Relativity: The GPS Navigation System
source.publisher: Ohio State University Department of Astronomy (Richard Pogge); corroborated by Penn State GEOG 862 'The Satellite Clock' and Neil Ashby, Relativity in the Global Positioning System, Living Reviews in Relativity

notes: At 20,200 km altitude gravity is weaker, so general relativity makes a satellite clock run about 45 microseconds per day FASTER than an identical clock on the ground. Travelling at 3.874 km/s (about 14,000 km/h), special relativity makes it run about 7 microseconds per day SLOWER. The two do not cancel: the net effect is a gain of about 38 microseconds per day. Values plotted are magnitudes; the signs are stated in the narration.
